messages:
lisa: Hey team, incoming escalation from ArcadiaHealth — multiple 502/504s reported for hosted-inference in eu-west between 04:10-04:30 UTC. Customer sees TLS handshake timeouts and gateway 502s. They said it started right after a cert rotation window. Sample curl output from their side:

lisa: ```
$ curl -v https://inference.redwood.example.com/v1/predict
*   Trying 198.51.100.23:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connection timed out after 30002 ms
* Closing connection 0
* TLS handshake timeout
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 30002 milliseconds with 0 out of -1 bytes received
```

lisa: And our gateway logs (short snippet):

lisa: ```
[2026-03-14T04:12:02Z] upstream connect error or disconnect, server: gw-eu-west-1, peer: 198.51.100.23:443, reason: TLS handshake timed out, requests: 42
[2026-03-14T04:12:04Z] route: /v1/predict, model: redwood-7b, token_cost: 0.12
```

michael: tagging infra — michael here. Can we get the resolver / DNS chain and a traceroute from the customer? Also want our edge pod metrics for connection churn/conntrack usage around that window.

lisa: Customer provided these outputs — pasted raw:

lisa: ```
$ dig +short inference.redwood.example.com A @8.8.8.8
198.51.100.23
198.51.100.45

$ dig +trace inference.redwood.example.com
;... -> returned two A records, one came from eu-west-1 pool (198.51.100.23) and one from a blue/alt pool (198.51.100.45)

$ traceroute 198.51.100.23
 1  10.0.0.1 (10.0.0.1)  1.12 ms
 2  203.0.113.254 (203.0.113.254)  10.5 ms
 3  * * *

# curl -v --resolve inference.redwood.example.com:443:198.51.100.45 https://inference.redwood.example.com/v1/predict
* Connected to 198.51.100.45 (198.51.100.45) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 handshake completed quickly
* HTTP/2 connection established
< 200 OK
```

michael: That is useful — traffic to .45 looks fine, .23 is the one timing out. ops-oncall, can you pull conntrack/ephemeral-ports stats for the gw-eu-west-1 fleet? I suspect NAT port starvation or very high churn for that POP.

ops-oncall: On it. Initial glance shows a spike in short-lived connections from ArcadiaHealth IP block ~04:10-04:18 UTC, conntrack table at gw-eu-west-1 was ~92% utilization. Also seeing retries from customers with very low TCP TIME_WAIT reuse.

ops-oncall: Quick mitigation idea: route ArcadiaHealth traffic to the blue pool (.45) via an emergency per-customer routing rule and ask them to retry. That bypasses the overloaded NAT at .23. I can flip the route now for a small subset.

ada: FYI: we simultaneously did a cert rotation at 04:15 UTC across the primary pool. If the DNS cache at some resolvers had a stale A record combined with a cert rotation, SNI could mismatch or the client might repeatedly retry the failing endpoint. Worth considering a collision between DNS rollout and cert rotate.

dns-team: We rolled a change to authoritative ns that introduced an additional A for the blue pool ~04:09 UTC with a 30s TTL. Some upstream resolvers held both A records and round-robin'd. We did not expect the primary pool to hit conntrack limits. Rolling back the change will remove .23 from answers for legacy resolvers that kept the stale mapping. Rolling back now.

lisa: Arcadia support confirms they're able to hit the endpoint after we routed them to .45:

arcadia-support: Confirmed — after you switched us to the alternate pool we saw immediate success, no 502s for 2 minutes. Thanks.

michael: Good. ops-oncall, keep .23 in drain for 10 mins and monitor conntrack and TLS handshake success rate. Also add a short-term increase to conntrack table on gw-eu-west-1 if possible (ops runbook step).

ops-oncall: Draining .23 now, conntrack limits increased by 20% on the affected nodes, moving additional capacity. Initial handshake success rate jumped from 78% -> 99% for Arcadia source IPs.

ada: Postmortem items:
- avoid simultaneous cert rotations + DNS rollouts for same pool (add a pre-check)
- add canary for conntrack exhaustion during DNS changes
- document per-customer emergency route steps in playbook

dns-team: rollback completed at 04:27 UTC; authoritative now serving only .45 for those resolvers that saw inconsistencies. We'll follow up with TTL tuning and add monitoring that alerts on A-record count divergence across resolvers.

lisa: Customer emailed back saying service is stable. I'll leave this open to confirm 1 hour. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Incident ticket INF-2026-482 created and linked to the postmortem doc: https://redwood.atlassian.example/INF-2026-482

lisa: Follow-ups assigned: dns-team -> add divergence alerts; infra -> conntrack scaling defaults; product -> update rotation playbook. Closing once stable for 1h.
